datum: The Lord will come, * and will not tarry; He both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make Himself manifest to all people. Alleluia.
Rejoice greatly, O Jerusalem, * for thy Saviour cometh unto thee. Alleluia.
I will place salvation in Zion, * and My glory in Jerusalem. Alleluia.
Every mountain and hill * shall be made low, and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come and make no tarrying. Alleluia.
We should live * righteously and godly, looking for that blessed hope and the coming of the Lord.
Before Me * there was no god formed, neither shall there be after Me; for unto Me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall swear.
O Lord, we beseech thee, mercifully incline thine ears unto our prayers, and lighten the darkness of our minds by the grace of thy heavenly visitation.

incipit: Behold, the Lord shall appear upon a white cloud,
responsum: And ten thousand of His saints with Him; and He shall have on His vesture, and on His thigh a name written King of kings, and Lord of lords.
versus: He shall appear and not lie; though He tarry, wait for Him, because He will surely come.

incipit: Thou, Bethlehem, art the city of the Most High God, out of thee shall He come forth That is to be Ruler in Israel; Whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting, and now shall He be great unto the ends of the earth.
responsum: And this Man shall be the peace in our land, when He shall come.
versus: He shall speak peace unto the Gentiles, and shall have dominion from sea to sea.

incipit: He That shall come, will come, and will not tarry; and there shall no more be fear in our borders.
versus: He shall tread down all our iniquities, and cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.

datum: Sermon by Pope St. Leo.

Dearly beloved brethren, with the care which becometh us as the shepherd of your souls, we urge upon you the rigid observance of this December Fast. The month of December hath come round again, and with it this devout custom of the Church. The fruits of the year, which is drawing to a close, are now all gathered in, and we most meetly offer our abstinence to God as a sacrifice of thanksgiving. And what can be more useful than fasting, that exercise by which we draw nigh to God, make a stand against the devil, and overcome the softer enticements of sin?

incipit: Weep not, O Egypt, for the Ruler cometh unto thee, and the depths shall be moved at His presence.
responsum: To deliver His people out of the hand of the mighty.
versus: Behold, the Lord of hosts, thy God, cometh with great power.

datum: Fasting hath ever been the bread of strength. From abstinence proceed pure thoughts, reasonable desires, and healthy counsels. By voluntary mortifications the flesh dieth to lust, and the soul is renewed in might. But since fasting is not the only mean whereby we get health for our souls, let us add to our fasting works of mercy. Let us spend in good deeds what we take from indulgence. Let our fast become the banquet of the poor.

incipit: Her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.
responsum: Lord shall have mercy on Jacob, and Israel shall be saved.
versus: Turn again, O Virgin of Israel, turn again to thy cities.

datum: Let us defend the widow and serve the orphan; let us comfort the afflicted and reconcile the estranged; let us take in the wanderer and succour the oppressed; let us clothe the naked and cherish the sick. And may every one of us that shall offer to the God of all goodness this Advent sacrifice of fasting and alms be by Him fitted to receive an eternal reward in His heavenly kingdom! We fast on Wednesday and Friday; and there is likewise a Vigil on Saturday at the Church of St. Peter, that by his good prayers we may the more effectually obtain what we ask for, through our Lord Jesus Christ, Who with the Father and the Holy Ghost, liveth and reigneth, God, world without end. Amen.

incipit: The Lord shall come down like rain upon a fleece.
responsum: In His days shall righteousness flourish, and abundance of peace.
versus: All the kings of the earth shall fall down before Him, all nations shall serve Him.

datum: A Lesson from the Holy Gospel according to John.
In that time were sent from Jerusalem priests and Levites to John, to ask him: Who art thou? And so on.
Homily by Pope St. Gregory.

Dearly beloved brethren, the first thing which striketh us in today's Gospel is the lowly-mindedness of John. He was so great that it was thought he might be the Christ; yet he soberly chose rather to seem only what he really was, than to let the belief of men invest him with a dignity which did not belong to him; for he confessed, and denied not, but confessed, I am not the Christ, at the same time he would not deny what he was in reality; and thus his very truth-speaking made him a member of Him Whose title he would not by falsehood take. In that he arrogated not to himself the name of Christ, he became a member of Christ. While he humbly strove to confess his own weakness, he earned by his simplicity a part in the grandeur of his Master.

incipit: O Lord, come, and make no tarrying loosen the bonds of thy people.
responsum: And gather together into their own land them that are scattered abroad.
versus: Stir up, O Lord, thy power, and come among us, to save us.

datum: In considering this subject we find an apparent contradiction between one of John's statements, and the saying of our Redeemer recorded in another part of the Gospel. (Matth. xvii. 10-12.) When His disciples asked our Lord regarding the coming of Elias, He answered: Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. And if ye will receive it, this (that is, John) is Elias. (Matth. xi. 14.) But when John was asked if he was Elias, he answered: I am not. How comes it then, dearly beloved brethren, that we find the Truth Itself asserting what the prophet of the Truth denied? It must evidently be that our Lord meant one thing and John another, when the Lord said, This is, and John, I am not. For how can he be the prophet of truth, if he speak not according to the word of Him Who is the Eternal Truth?

incipit: Behold, there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall come for salvation unto the people, to it shall the Gentiles seek;
responsum: And His name shall be glorious.
versus: The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.

datum: Let us then more minutely examine these words, and we shall find that there is no real contradiction. When the Angel announced to Zacharias the coming birth of John he said He shall go before Him in the spirit and power of Elias, (Luke i. 17.) As the old Elias will come again before the Second Advent of the Lord, so did John, as the new Elias, go before the First Advent, in the spirit and power of Elias. As the old Elias will be the Fore-runner of the Judge, so the new Elias was the Forerunner of the Saviour. John then was Elias in spirit, but not in person; and our Lord asserteth of the spirit what John denieth of the person.

incipit: The Lord will teach us of His ways, and we will walk in His paths.
responsum: For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
versus: Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob.

datum: He shall sit * upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom for ever. Alleluia.
Blessed art thou, * O Mary, who hast believed the Lord, for there shall be a performance of those things which were told thee from the Lord. Alleluia.
There shall come forth a rod * out of the stem of Jesse, and the whole earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
All generations shall call me blessed, * for God hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden.
Thou, Bethlehem, * in the land of Judah, shalt not be the least (among the princes of Judah) for out of thee shall come a Ruler, That shall rule my people Israel.
Awake, awake, * arise, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion.

incipit: The Lord shall go forth and fight against the nations.
responsum: And His feet shall stand upon the mount of Olives on the east.
versus: And it shall be exalted above the hills, and all nations shall flow unto it.

incipit: The Fore-runner is for us entered, even the Lamb without spot
responsum: Made an High Priest for ever after the order of Melchisedek.
versus: This is that King of Righteousness without descent, nor end of life.

incipit: The Gentiles shall see thy Righteous One, and all kings thy Glorious one.
responsum: And thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord hath named.
versus: Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.

datum: Let your soul watch, * the Lord our God is nigh at hand.
Rejoice ye with Jerusalem, * and be glad with her, all ye that love her for ever.
